formula: change_mass_pos ~ n_words * status_gini * centrality_gini * speaker_gini + (1 | movie)
notes: Read deposit page (paper model 2 as filed) and conversation_r.R: global model of the MuMIn dredge on the Gini predictors, final models refit with (1|movie) on the z-scored copy (osf_15). Neural alignment is change_mass_pos; the second DV mean_vector_change (behavioural alignment, same structure) is in ignore. The table also has a group column (9 groups, crossed with movie) that the dredge global model used as (1|group); the filed model and the paper's results use movie only, so group is neither grouping factor nor ignored.

Paper text (results, whole-brain alignment): mixed model of meaning change on whole-brain alignment with random intercepts for participant pairs; alignment is the sum of unthresholded positive change in ISC, taken here as pos_mass. The pair term is the combination of the two participant ids. The practice survey did not row this model (it names it among the further pair-level LMMs with (1|pair)); the analysis script for it is not rendered on the deposit page. run_num is the movie clip. meaning_change is missing for some rows.

formula: pos_mass ~ eigencent_ego + eigencent_alter + brokerage_ego + brokerage_alter + (1 | subj_id_ego:subj_id_alter)
notes: Paper text (results, neural influence): mixed model of ego and alter eigenvector centrality and brokerage on whole-brain neural influence with random intercepts for participant pairs, pairs only if in the same conversation group (the talked column). The same-structure model with centrality_ego and centrality_alter (PCA centrality) is the same model with other covariates and not a second row. Neural influence taken as pos_mass and survey influence as meaning_pull (ignored); the practice survey did not row this model and its script is not rendered. RULE GAP: ordered ego-alter pairs share one paper pair, the term subj_id_ego:subj_id_alter treats (A,B) and (B,A) as two pairs.

Paper model 4 as filed (status_z ~ participant + (1|rater)); analysis.py fits smf.mixedlm(status ~ 1 + sid, groups=rater) on the stacked status ratings. status_z is the z-scored Social status, so the raw column is the response. 390 ratings of 39 participants by 10 raters; Subject ID is a fixed factor, Group and Speaker ID are not in the model.
